serviceIdentification.serviceName: IronWiFi Cloud RADIUS and Wi-Fi Authentication Platform
serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
**IronWiFi is the vendor-neutral authentication layer for agency Wi-Fi and wired networks: cloud RADIUS, 802.1X with EAP-TLS, cloud PKI with SCEP enrollment, captive portals, and Wi-Fi identity threat detection (ITDR), delivered as SaaS on Google Cloud with US regions available.**

**Keep the network you have.** IronWiFi works with any access point, switch or controller that speaks RADIUS and 802.1X, so an agency adds certificate-based authentication and policy without replacing hardware or running RADIUS and NPS servers on premises.

**Use the identities you already manage.** Users and devices authenticate against Microsoft Entra ID (commercial and GCC High), Google Workspace, Okta, and LDAP or Active Directory. Device certificates are issued and renewed by the built-in cloud PKI over SCEP, including for MDM-managed fleets.

**See who and what is on the network.** Every authentication is logged per user and device; the ITDR service flags credential misuse, rogue devices and anomalous access on Wi-Fi and reports through the console, API and webhooks.

**Guest, visitor and roaming access** through branded captive portals, vouchers, sponsored access and OpenRoaming, on the same platform.

**Assurance on record.** SOC 2 Type II (Johanson Group LLP, report issued 7 May 2026) held in the IronWiFi Trust Center. FIPS 199 impact categorization Moderate (this is not a FedRAMP Moderate Authorization). IronWiFi-prepared 20x Class A package documents were published 13 September 2026 and the 20x Class A Certification application (FRC-APP-AFC) was submitted to FedRAMP the same day; FedRAMP's decision is pending. Marketplace status is Not yet certified and Certification Class is Unknown until FedRAMP records it. IronWiFi is in the Initial Implementation Phase and is not FedRAMP Certified today.

**Agency use cases:** direct use as the authentication, policy and monitoring layer inside an agency information system; indirect use as a third-party information resource inside integrator and managed-service offerings delivered to agencies. Documentation, a REST API and a self-service console let an agency pilot the service on its existing network.

trustCenter.repositoryDescription: IronWiFi Trust Center hosting SOC 2 Type II / SOC 3 reports, security control and subprocessor listings, and FedRAMP Certification Data for this offering.
trustCenter.accessRequestInstructions: The Trust Center landing page and its Controls and Subprocessors sections are open, no account required. Under Resources, the SOC 3 report, Data Processing Agreement and Terms of Service open directly. The FedRAMP Documentation category holds the certification package: the FedRAMP Public Information link opens directly, and the complete package bundle (every package file plus its SHA-256 manifest, as one zip) is downloadable without an account from the website URL listed under documentationOverview. The individual package documents in that category (Security Decision Record in PDF and JSON, Certification Package Overview PDF, Key Security Indicator Summary PDF, example Ongoing Certification Report in PDF and JSON, component inventory with its method and script, and the manifest) are released on request: select Request access on the resource; requests are reviewed and access is granted to the requesting email address. The SOC 2 Type II report is released the same way under a non-disclosure agreement. Questions about a request, or requests from federal agencies that need a different route, go to security@ironwifi.com.

additionalRepositories.repositoryDescription: IronWiFi Help Center: administrator and end-user documentation covering tenant setup, identity provider integration, RADIUS and certificate configuration, captive portal design, per-vendor wireless hardware setup guides, and troubleshooting.
IronWiFi REST API and webhook reference for automating tenant, network, user, certificate, and reporting operations.

secureConfigurationGuidance.repositoryDescription: Secure Configuration Guide for federal deployments of IronWiFi (version 1.1, 2026-09-13): the tenant owner and privileged accounts, secure access, configuration, operation and decommissioning, secure defaults at provisioning, and the recommended tenant configuration (operator identity and SSO enforcement, RADIUS and EAP method selection, RadSec, certificate lifecycle, logging and ITDR alerting). Machine-readable form at https://www.ironwifi.com/fedramp/secure-configuration/secure-configuration.json.

certifiedServices.serviceDescription: The administrative console for the offering: tenants, networks, users, certificates, reports and role-based access.

Multi-region RADIUS and RadSec authenticating users and devices with EAP-TLS, PEAP/MSCHAPv2, EAP-TTLS and MAC-based methods against Entra ID (commercial and GCC High Graph sync), Google Workspace, Okta and LDAP/Active Directory; per-network policy, VLAN and attribute assignment.
Branded captive portals with self-registration, vouchers, sponsored guest access, social and enterprise identity sign-in, terms acceptance and session control.
802.1X WPA-Enterprise authentication using the Cloud RADIUS service, including certificate-based EAP-TLS.
Built-in certificate authority issuing and renewing device and user certificates for EAP-TLS.
End-user and device enrollment into the tenant certificate authority.
Self-service device certificate and identity management for end users.
SCEP enrollment of device certificates through mobile device management.
Certificate or MAC-based authentication for IoT and non-user devices.
Passpoint / Hotspot 2.0 profiles so managed devices join participating networks automatically.
OpenRoaming federation RADIUS so managed devices authenticate on participating networks.
Wi-Fi calling authentication offload through the Cloud RADIUS service.
Authentication and session analytics in the administrative console.
Operator-facing analytics and assistance in the administrative console; does not change the authentication boundary.
REST API and webhooks for automating tenants, networks, users, certificates and reports.
Per-network policy that decides whether a user or device is admitted and which VLAN or attributes apply.
Directory and SCIM provisioning of users into the offering.
Detection of credential misuse, rogue and anomalous devices and abnormal access patterns, with alerts to the console, API and webhooks.
Terraform provider for automating tenant, network and policy configuration through the REST API.
Analytics for OpenRoaming and Passpoint federation sessions.

certified.name: Google Services (Google Cloud Platform Products and underlying Infrastructure)
certified.certificationClass: Rev5, JAB path, Class D (High); FedRAMP Certified, listed since 2019-12-04
certified.useCase: Hosting for every service: Cloud Spanner, Cloud Run, Compute Engine, App Engine, BigQuery, Cloud Logging.
certified.inheritance: Not claimed. The offering does not run in an Assured Workloads environment, so FedRAMP-authorized regions and controls are not enforced at the project level; Google Cloud is recorded here as the certified third-party resource that hosts the offering, and the justification, mitigations and compensating controls are in the Certification Package Overview.

nonCertified.name: Stripe
nonCertified.useCase: Subscription billing for operator accounts (console services only).

nonCertified.name: SendGrid
nonCertified.useCase: Transactional email: operator alerts and account mail; scheduled reports are delivered as GCS signed links, with an attachment fallback only when the upload fails.

nonCertified.name: Twilio
nonCertified.useCase: SMS verification for guest network access. The destination number is sent to Twilio as the SMS recipient and is retained on the IronWiFi user record (captive-portal services only).

nonCertified.name: Bugsnag
nonCertified.useCase: Error tracking on five captive-portal services with tenancy identifiers redacted, plus a browser client still present on live console pages; removal in progress as of 2026-09-13.

nonCertified.name: Have I Been Pwned
nonCertified.useCase: Breached-password check on password set and reset using k-anonymity; no identifier leaves the platform.

nonCertified.name: Cloudflare
nonCertified.useCase: Performance and DDoS protection for the public marketing website only; no customer data transits Cloudflare.

nonCertified.name: GitHub
nonCertified.useCase: Source control and CI; no customer data, in scope for deployment integrity.

nonCertified.name: HubSpot
nonCertified.useCase: Customer-enabled captive-portal lead capture. Guest contacts are sent to the tenant's own HubSpot account under a token the tenant supplies; IronWiFi holds no HubSpot credential. Not an IronWiFi subprocessor.

nonCertified.name: Mailchimp
nonCertified.useCase: Customer-enabled captive-portal list sync. Guest contacts are sent to the tenant's own Mailchimp audience under a token the tenant supplies; IronWiFi holds no Mailchimp credential. Not an IronWiFi subprocessor.

excludedFromMinimumAssessmentScope.exclusionRationale: Fronted by Cloudflare, separate from the platform; handles no customer data of the offering and does not affect the confidentiality, integrity or availability of data the offering handles.
Hosted documentation; handles no customer data of the offering.
Reports on the offering rather than being used by it. Hosted by UptimeRobot, deliberately outside the boundary so availability information stays reachable during a disruption.
Hosted by Vanta; publishes certification data and audit reports and records access requests, but handles no customer data of the offering.

alternativeSecurityFramework.note: IronWiFi applied on 2026-09-13 for FedRAMP 20x Class A using an alternative security framework (FRC-CLA-ASF) rather than a FedRAMP independent assessment. No FedRAMP Recognized assessor is engaged, as none is required at Class A, so the schema's assessor property is omitted; the decision on engaging one for a higher class is due by the third quarter of 2027 (see Certification progress on the public page). Marketplace Certification Class remains Unknown until FedRAMP decides the application and records a class.
alternativeSecurityFramework.nextReportExpected: Six to eight weeks after 2027-02-28, targeted before 2027-05-07 so that a current report is always within 12 months of the last; Statement of Work executed 2026-09-07.

informationFlows.summary: Operators, end users, network devices and API clients reach the offering over the public internet through TLS 1.2 or higher terminated at the Google edge. The console API and single-page application run on Cloud Run in eleven regions and talk to Cloud Spanner (a global database for operator accounts, OAuth clients and settings; regional databases, selected by hostname, for end users, networks, devices and RADIUS secrets), Redis for sessions and rate limiting, and BigQuery for request logs and usage metrics. RADIUS, RadSec, captive portal, PKI and SCEP services receive authentication and enrolment requests from network and end-user devices, consult the tenant's identity provider (Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta or LDAP) where configured, and return results to the network; the identity threat detection pipeline is derived from those authentication and accounting events. Scheduled reports, connector syncs and cleanup run as internal task workers. Tenant data is stored in the region the tenant selects; all data at rest is encrypted with Google-managed AES-256 and all transit is TLS.
informationFlows.securityCategories: All twenty services in this offering are categorized under FIPS 199 as Confidentiality Moderate, Integrity Moderate, Availability Low, overall Moderate (approved by the accountable official 2026-08-24). FIPS 199 Moderate is an impact categorization; it is not a FedRAMP Moderate Authorization and it is not a 20x Class C certification. No information resource within the Minimum Assessment Scope carries a different categorization; the resources under excludedFromMinimumAssessmentScope carry none because they handle no customer data of the offering. Device Trust is marketed as Coming Soon and is not one of the twenty services.
informationFlows.detailedDiagrams: The information flow and categorization document (information-flows-and-categories.md, built from the platform data flow diagram) and the machine-readable component inventory are part of the certification package; the inventory is released on request through the Trust Center and is in the public package bundle, and the flow document is supplied to federal agencies and FedRAMP on request to security@ironwifi.com.

documentationOverview.description: Documentation supplied by IronWiFi for the offering, as CDS-CSO-PUB item 13 requires. The Certification Package Overview (this JSON and its page), the public FedRAMP page, the secure configuration guidance and the complete package bundle are readable without an account; the individual package documents and the SOC 2 Type II report are released on request through the Trust Center.

packageMetadata.schemaNote: CPO-CSO-MTD requires this metadata in the Certification Package Overview. The published schema (fedramp-certification-package-overview-schema-2026-06-24) defines no property for it, so it is carried here as a declared object; extra fields do not fail FedRAMP schema validation. The accountable official's role address is also recorded under contactInformation.
